output.name: Ruhkan

anatomy.part: heel of the palm, left side
heel of the palm, right side
wrist, where the arm leaves the frame
tip of the little finger, pinned above the north
the kite, on its string from the palm

output.myth: Ruhk made kites for the whole Windward coast, and in the hard winter of the long salt his fingers went white and then black, and three came off at the second knuckle. Ruhk did not sit down about it. He pricked his stumps through the cloth with a bone needle, bound them with gut, and went on stitching. His kites never tore. Not once. Tavo, the Gale, who tears everything, came down the coast to see for himself and found no seam to pull. He laughed until the cliffs rang, then went looking for a better game. Mother Hesk saw the hand Ruhk held up to the wind and counted it. When Ruhk went aloft, Ennu pinned his hand above the north where Hesk could wind it, and it is still there, open, holding a kite string that goes down into the dark. Children who fly badly are told to ask Ruhk for steady hands.
output.verse:
Three fingers gone white,
he stitched with the stumps and kept
the north holds his hand.
